newsitem.title: USA: Mercantile says Q1 earnings unsatisfactory.
newsitem.headline: Mercantile says Q1 earnings unsatisfactory.

text.p: Mercantile Stores Co Inc said on Monday its first quarter earnings report was "less than satisfactory", and comparable store sales productivity in the quarter was disappointing.

The company reported first quarter net per share of $0.52, up from $0.36 in the year ago period. The 1996 quarter included an after tax charge of $7.2 million, or $0.20 per share reflecting the adoption of a new accounting standard related to the impairment of long-lived assets.

Retail sales, which exclude finance charge revenues, rose 4.4 percent in the first quarter to $661 million compared with the year ago period. Sales in comparable units increased 1.3 percent in the period.
The company said it had expected a difficult first quarter of 1997 because it was going against a strong comparable quarter from last year, when same store sales increased over six percent.

The company also said it had to underwrite the losses which new stores traditionally report in their first full year of operation. The new stores which were opened toward the end of 1996 produced a net loss of $2.5 million, or $.07 per share, in the quarter.

"We must, however, look to the disappointing comparable store sales productivity in the quarter as being a negative contributor to this earnings report which we consider less than satisfactory, " chairman and chief executive officer, David L. Nichols said.
